intents.name: Cache Locality Optimization
intents.description: Improve data reuse by structuring computation to fit working sets within L1/L2 cache hierarchies.
intents.rationale: Convolution has high arithmetic intensity but poor spatial locality by default due to strided access patterns across input channels and spatial dimensions. Tiling ensures that input/filter/output tiles fit in cache, reducing memory bandwidth pressure on Broadwell's cache hierarchy.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition loop iterations into smaller blocks that operate on cache-sized data tiles.
transformations.rationale: Enables reuse of input and filter data across multiple output computations by constraining working set size to L1/L2 capacity.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Copy and reorganize data into contiguous, cache-line-aligned buffers optimized for the tiled computation order.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates strided memory access within tiles, improving cache line utilization and prefetcher effectiveness for the NCHW/FCHW layout.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder loop nests to change the iteration order of dimensions.
transformations.rationale: Positions loops to maximize temporal locality; e.g., iterating over output channels in inner loops can improve filter reuse.

transformations.name: Fusion
transformations.description: Combine producer-consumer operations to avoid intermediate materialization.
transformations.rationale: If subsequent operations exist (e.g., bias add, activation), fusing them with convolution keeps output tiles in cache rather than spilling to memory.

intents.name: SIMD Vectorization
intents.description: Expose data-parallel operations to AVX2 vector units for throughput multiplication.
intents.rationale: The Broadwell E5-2680 v4 supports AVX2+FMA with 256-bit vectors (4 FP64 lanes). Convolution's innermost reductions and output accumulations are naturally vectorizable, but require proper loop structure and memory alignment.

transformations.name: Vectorization
transformations.description: Transform scalar loop iterations into SIMD vector operations.
transformations.rationale: Multiplies throughput by vector width (4x for FP64 AVX2); critical for achieving peak FLOPS on compute-bound convolution.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder loops to place vectorizable dimensions innermost.
transformations.rationale: Ensures contiguous memory access along the vectorized dimension, enabling efficient vector loads/stores without gather/scatter.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Reorganize data layout to ensure vector-width-aligned, contiguous access patterns.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates unaligned loads and enables full-width vector operations without masking overhead.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Replicate loop body multiple times to increase instruction-level parallelism.
transformations.rationale: Exposes more independent FMA operations to hide latency and saturate vector execution units.

intents.name: Parallelization
intents.description: Distribute work across multiple cores to utilize the 28-core, 2-socket NUMA topology.
intents.rationale: Single-threaded execution underutilizes the E5-2680 v4's massive core count. Batch and output channel dimensions offer embarrassingly parallel work that scales linearly with cores.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Mark loop dimensions for concurrent execution across threads.
transformations.rationale: Batch (N) and output filter (F) dimensions have no cross-iteration dependencies, enabling straightforward parallel distribution.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition work into coarse-grained chunks suitable for thread assignment.
transformations.rationale: Creates balanced work units that minimize synchronization overhead and enable NUMA-local memory allocation.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Position parallel loops at outermost levels of the loop nest.
transformations.rationale: Maximizes work per parallel task and minimizes thread management overhead by parallelizing coarse-grained outer loops.

intents.name: Register Pressure Management
intents.description: Balance unrolling and tiling to maximize register utilization without causing spills.
intents.rationale: Broadwell has 16 YMM registers for AVX2. Aggressive unrolling can exhaust registers, causing spills that negate vectorization benefits. Careful tuning is essential for FP64 convolution with its large accumulator state.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Replicate loop iterations to increase register-resident computation.
transformations.rationale: Keeps accumulator values in registers across multiple FMA operations, amortizing load/store costs.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Control tile sizes to bound the number of live values requiring registers.
transformations.rationale: Smaller micro-tiles reduce simultaneous accumulator count, preventing register spills while maintaining locality.

transformations.name: Peeling
transformations.description: Separate edge iterations from main loop body to simplify the main kernel.
transformations.rationale: Removes boundary condition checks from the hot path, enabling more aggressive register allocation in the main loop.

intents.name: Kernel Decomposition
intents.description: Break down the 7-deep convolution loop nest into simpler, more optimizable sub-operations.
intents.rationale: Direct convolution with NCHW/FCHW layout has complex strided access. Decomposition exposes matrix-multiply-like structure that benefits from highly optimized GEMM-style transformations.

transformations.name: Decomposition
transformations.description: Split compound operations into sequences of simpler operations.
transformations.rationale: Separates reduction dimensions from spatial dimensions, enabling independent optimization of each phase.

transformations.name: Im2col Transformation
transformations.description: Reshape convolution into matrix multiplication by explicit input unfolding.
transformations.rationale: Converts strided convolution access into contiguous GEMM, enabling use of cache-optimized matrix multiplication strategies.

transformations.name: Fusion
transformations.description: Recombine decomposed operations to avoid intermediate materialization overhead.
transformations.rationale: After optimizing sub-operations, selective fusion can eliminate memory traffic for intermediate buffers.

intents.name: Memory Layout Optimization
intents.description: Transform data layouts to improve access patterns for the target loop structure.
intents.rationale: NCHW layout causes strided access across the width dimension during convolution. Layout transformation can convert these into contiguous accesses, dramatically improving cache and vector efficiency.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Create temporary buffers with computation-friendly data layouts.
transformations.rationale: Converts NCHW/FCHW into blocked layouts (e.g., NCHWc) that align with tile boundaries and vector widths.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition dimensions to create natural boundaries for layout transformation.
transformations.rationale: Tile sizes determine block factors in packed layouts, coordinating memory organization with computation structure.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder iteration to match the transformed data layout.
transformations.rationale: Ensures innermost loops traverse contiguous packed data, maximizing cache line utilization.

intents.name: Reduction Optimization
intents.description: Optimize the accumulation over input channels and kernel spatial dimensions.
intents.rationale: Convolution reduces over C, KH, KW dimensions. Inefficient reduction order causes repeated loads of output accumulators. Proper structuring keeps accumulators register-resident.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Position reduction loops to maximize accumulator reuse.
transformations.rationale: Placing channel reduction innermost allows output tile accumulators to remain in registers across all C iterations.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition reduction dimensions to balance parallelism and accumulator locality.
transformations.rationale: Tiled reductions enable parallel partial sums while controlling the number of concurrent accumulators.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Unroll reduction loops to expose FMA chains.
transformations.rationale: Creates longer dependency chains that the out-of-order engine can overlap, hiding FMA latency.

intents.name: NUMA-Aware Optimization
intents.description: Structure computation and data placement to respect the 2-socket NUMA topology.
intents.rationale: Cross-socket memory access incurs significant latency penalty on dual-socket Broadwell. Large tensors spanning both NUMA nodes require careful work distribution to maintain locality.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Create coarse tiles aligned with NUMA-local memory regions.
transformations.rationale: Ensures each socket processes data residing in its local memory, avoiding QPI interconnect traffic.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Distribute parallel work to match NUMA topology.
transformations.rationale: Socket-aware thread binding ensures threads access predominantly local memory, reducing average memory latency.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Allocate packed buffers in NUMA-local memory.
transformations.rationale: First-touch allocation during packing ensures working buffers reside on the correct NUMA node.

intents.name: Loop Canonicalization
intents.description: Normalize loop structure to enable downstream transformations.
intents.rationale: Many transformations have preconditions on loop form (normalized bounds, single induction variable). Canonicalization ensures the IR is in a state amenable to tiling, vectorization, and parallelization.

transformations.name: Canonicalization
transformations.description: Apply standard simplifications and normalizations to the IR.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates redundant operations and normalizes loop bounds, creating a clean foundation for optimization.

transformations.name: Peeling
transformations.description: Extract boundary iterations to create perfectly nested main loops.
transformations.rationale: Separates irregular edge cases from the main computation, enabling more aggressive optimization of the common path.

transformations.name: Loop Coalescing
transformations.description: Merge multiple loops into a single loop when beneficial.
transformations.rationale: Simplifies loop structure for certain parallelization and vectorization strategies.

intents.name: Prefetch Optimization
intents.description: Improve memory access latency hiding through explicit or implicit prefetching.
intents.rationale: Convolution's regular access patterns are prefetcher-friendly, but large strides across channels can defeat hardware prefetch. Explicit hints or access restructuring can improve memory subsystem utilization.

transformations.name: Software Prefetching
transformations.description: Insert explicit prefetch instructions ahead of data use.
transformations.rationale: Compensates for hardware prefetcher limitations with large strides by explicitly initiating cache line fetches.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Reorganize data to create sequential access patterns.
transformations.rationale: Converts strided accesses into sequential streaming patterns that hardware prefetchers can track effectively.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Increase loop body size to provide more prefetch distance.
transformations.rationale: Creates sufficient distance between prefetch and use, allowing memory latency to be fully hidden.
